messages:
Li_CorpInfra: Hey team — we've got a nasty one from our on-prem product. Streaming SSE responses from our Dedicated deployment keep cutting off mid-event, clients reconnect, then sometimes the resumed request gets 401. Happens only when traffic flows through our corporate proxy + on‑prem ingress. RR happened across multiple users.

Li_CorpInfra: Details: private/dedicated, VPC MTU is 1400 (corporate WAN shrinks MSS), corp proxy is "BlueCo Proxy" (middleware doing SSL/TLS inspection), onprem ingress uses HAProxy 2.0. Token rotation every 5m (short TTL). SDK uses automatic reconnect/resume logic.

Maya_support: thanks Li — can you share a minimal repro curl and a short example of the truncated output? also confirm whether non-streaming (batch) responses are fine.

Li_CorpInfra: Non-streaming generate endpoint works fine. Streaming example (token sanitized):
```bash
curl -v --http1.1 --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" https://private.redwood.example/v1/stream
```
Sample truncated chunk from client log: `data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"The quick br` — then connection dies, client reconnects and gets `401 Bearer` even though token should still be valid for another 60s.

Arjun_eng-infra: couple of thoughts: 1) MTU/MSS clamping on corporate path can split TLS records/chunk boundaries such that the proxy or HAProxy temp buffers create an incomplete SSE event when the client sees it. If the SDK resume expects to re-attach to a message boundary it can get confused. 2) BlueCo's TLS inspection may terminate and re-open sessions, and if token rotation happens between the original stream and the resumed connection the resumed request will legitimately 401.

Jo_sre: +1. We see a lot of symptoms where `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` chunks get cut at MTU and some proxies aggressively buffer and flush partial chunks. Also some proxies will inject or strip `Connection` headers. Would like: a pcap of the session and the HAProxy/proxy logs around the disconnect.

Maya_support: Li, can you gather: 1) client raw stdout of curl command (with `--no-buffer`), 2) a short tcpdump from the client side around the failure (tcpdump -w), 3) proxy/access logs for the timeframe. If you prefer, we can provide instructions for a lighter repro to run in your env.

Li_CorpInfra: attaching short curl dump inline (sanitized):
```
> GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1
> Host: private.redwood.example
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
> Accept: text/event-stream
> 
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< content-type: text/event-stream
< transfer-encoding: chunked
< 
data: {"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"The quick br
```
then 3s later connection closed. client reconnects, we see new request with same Bearer header and get `HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized` for the resumed stream.

Arjun_eng-infra: can you also try forcing http/1.1 on the client with `--http1.1` (you already do), and try `--no-keepalive` to see if the proxy behaves differently. For nginx proxies the typical fixes are: `proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection ""; proxy_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on; proxy_buffer_size 16k; proxy_read_timeout 120s;` — these reduce proxy reassembly and buffering that cause partial events. For HAProxy, ensure `option http-server-close` or `option http-keep-alive` set intentionally and increase `tune.bufsize`.

Jo_sre: also check whether the proxy is doing body inspection that performs a read-ahead and then stalls on streaming bodies. That causes client to see a socket close while backend still sending.

Nora_account: Li — I see you're on a Dedicated plan with reserved capacity. we can spin up a short test endpoint in our infra (same region) to reproduce without the corp proxy in the path — would you like us to do that as a controlled isolator?

Li_CorpInfra: yes please. that would help isolate. We can also run tcpdump next week.

Arjun_eng-infra: additional low-friction repro steps for you to try locally: 1) curl to our test (we provide url) with `--no-buffer --http1.1`, 2) try using `openssl s_client -quiet -connect private.redwood.example:443` and paste raw bytes you see — you can sometimes spot chunk boundaries there, 3) if you control the corp proxy, temporarily increase proxy buffer size or disable request/response body inspection.

Maya_support: quick mitigation if you cannot change proxy: a) use non-streaming endpoint for critical flows, b) increase client retry backoff and re-fetch from start-of-message (idempotent) instead of relying on internal resume token, c) increase token TTL during streaming sessions (we can whitelist a longer-lived token for testing).

Li_CorpInfra: are there known issues on Redwood side where resume fails with 401? Could the resume token be tied to the original TLS session?

Arjun_eng-infra: resume should be stateless and based on a resume token in the payload/headers, not tied to TLS session. However, we do have a safety that rotates auth sessions for connections that abruptly close if token rotation policy is aggressive; that can cause resumption to require a fresh auth exchange. I'll check code paths — tagging @deploy-bot to pull relevant deploy logs.

deploy-bot: pulled recent stream-resume commits (last 30 days). No active rollouts affecting resume token handshake.

Jo_sre: next actionable items: 1) Li capture pcap + curl stdout + proxy logs and upload (we'll provide secure presigned S3), 2) Redwood infra will stand up an isolated test stream without the corp proxy to verify whether server emits full events, 3) if we reproduce proxy-induced truncation we can craft a doc for corp proxy configs (nginx/haproxy) to avoid SSE truncation.

Li_CorpInfra: capturing now. one extra datapoint: when the resume 401 happens, the corp proxy logs show an upstream 200 followed by immediate new connection from client — no explicit 401 logged by proxy (so 401 likely from backend on the resumed request).

Arjun_eng-infra: that matches token-rotation race. If the backend rotated the short-lived token store (e.g., revoking old resume tokens), the resumed connection may be rejected. For now, we can: 1) increase resume token grace window on backend for your org (temporary config change), 2) surface a clearer error in the SDK so it retries refresh+resend instead of surfacing 401 to app. I'll file follow-up to eng to add more graceful resume handling.

Maya_support: Li — we'll provision the isolated test and share the URL. After you upload pcap and logs, we'll run comparisons and propose either (A) proxy config changes (nginx/haproxy snippets), or (B) SDK change to try token refresh automatically on 401 during resume, or (C) short-term token grace for your org.

Li_CorpInfra: thanks. I'll upload pcap + proxy logs to the presigned link in ~2 hours. One more question: would adding application-level periodic heartbeats (SSE `event: heartbeat`) help?

Jo_sre: yes — heartbeats every 10-15s keep the proxy from deciding the stream is idle and can reduce 50/60s idle timeouts. They also help the client detect mid-event stalls earlier. We'll recommend heartbeat as a short-term hedge.

Maya_support: +1. We'll also send a small nginx/haproxy doc with exact knobs we've used for other customers.

Li_CorpInfra: uploaded files (pcap, curl_dump.txt, proxy_access.log). Thanks everyone, standing by for the isolated test endpoint.

Maya_support: got them — thanks. @Arjun_eng-infra @Jo_sre we'll analyze and try to reproduce in the isolated environment. I'll follow up in this thread with remediation steps and the nginx/haproxy snippets. :thumbsup:

Arjun_eng-infra: preliminary note for the internal runbook I'll add: check for MTU/MSS<->TLS record fragmentation + proxy body inspection + short token TTL. Those three combined are the usual culprit for truncated SSE+401 on resume.

Maya_support: closing loop: scheduling a 1:1 debug with Li tomorrow to watch a repro in real time. We'll keep thread updated.

Li_CorpInfra: thanks, appreciate the quick triage.
